frase_inicial: Daniel and Emily: together you already bring in $280,000 a year — and there is a clear, calm path forward.

tarjetas.frente: Your short cash cushion leaves daily life exposed
tarjetas.reverso: If a paycheck paused tomorrow, the kids’ routine could still keep going for a short time, but you’d likely reach for the high-rate card. Building accessible cash first buys breathing room and avoids adding costly debt.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash: $19,000 today; recommended emergency reserve: $106,860–$120,217; shortfall to adjusted min with near-term goals: $92,360.

tarjetas.frente: Life cover is far below what protects your mortgage and children
tarjetas.reverso: If one of you died, the remaining partner would face the mortgage, car loan and college costs. Raising life cover in steps can secure the kids’ schooling and the home without changing everything at once.
tarjetas.detalle: Daniel life cover: $250,000 (shortfall ~$1,350,000). Emily life cover: $200,000 (shortfall ~$1,000,000). Top move suggests adding $1,166,000 life cover.

tarjetas.frente: No umbrella policy means one big claim could reach your savings
tarjetas.reverso: A liability claim could touch your home and future earnings. Adding umbrella cover creates a layer that keeps big bills off your savings and from forcing hard trade-offs between goals.
tarjetas.detalle: Plan identifies no umbrella; recommended minimum $1,000,000 gap. Combined move (life + umbrella) lifts score to 60.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement saving is the largest long-term gap
tarjetas.reverso: Right now nothing goes into your workplace retirement accounts, so retirement relies heavily on future income. You can decide the pace: small regular steps now, larger changes later if you both agree.
tarjetas.detalle: Required extra retirement saving ~ $34,165/yr; net cash flow this year available $15,032/yr. Employer match availability is unconfirmed.

tarjetas.frente: The credit card is the costliest debt dragging your cash
tarjetas.reverso: At current payments the card is projected to finish in a few years, but its high cost eats money now. A modest increase in monthly payment would cut interest and free cash for other priorities.
tarjetas.detalle: Credit card balance $18,000 at 24.9%, monthly payment $450, interest portion ~$373.50 of current payment.
